questions.q: What does this lesson say about Flashback's relationship to SQL Server features?
options: Flashback has no direct SQL Server equivalent; Temporal Tables are the nearest concept but cover much less
Flashback is functionally identical to SQL Server Temporal Tables
Flashback is a marketing name for SQL Server's backup and restore process
SQL Server has an exact feature called Flashback Database
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames Flashback as a genuinely distinctive Oracle capability, not a relabeled SQL Server feature.

questions.q: What does Flashback Query require in advance to work?
options: Nothing — it relies on Oracle's undo mechanism, which retains recent history by default
ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK ON must be run first
A Fast Recovery Area must be configured
The target table must have ENABLE ROW MOVEMENT set
questions.explain: Flashback Query works via undo with no per-object or database-level setup, as long as enough undo has been retained.

questions.q: What does FLASHBACK TABLE actually do, compared to Flashback Query?
options: It reverts the table's rows in place to a past point, rather than just reading a historical view
It only works on tables inside the recycle bin
It performs the same action as Flashback Query, just with different syntax
It requires a full RMAN restore first
questions.explain: Flashback Table changes the table's actual data, unlike Flashback Query which only reads a past version.

questions.q: What must be configured in advance for FLASHBACK DATABASE to be usable?
options: Flashback logging must be enabled and a Fast Recovery Area must exist to hold flashback logs
Nothing — it works identically to Flashback Query with zero setup
The recycle bin must be disabled
UNDO_RETENTION must be set to UNLIMITED
questions.explain: Unlike Flashback Query, Flashback Database requires ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK ON and a Fast Recovery Area configured ahead of time.

questions.q: Why is Flashback Database typically faster than an RMAN restore-and-recover to the same point in time?
options: It applies flashback logs rather than replaying every archived redo log from a backup forward
It skips reading any logs at all
It only works on a single tablespace, so there's less to process
RMAN restores are always slower than Data Pump imports
questions.explain: Flashback Database uses a purpose-built flashback log mechanism, which is faster than a full restore-and-recover cycle for undoing recent, widespread changes.
